content: Aluminium iodide refers to any chemical compound composed solely of aluminium and iodine. Typically, the term is used to describe aluminium triiodide (AlI₃), which is produced through the reaction of aluminium with iodine or by the action of hydrogen iodide (HI) on aluminium metal. In organic synthesis, aluminium iodide is utilized for its ability to cleave specific types of chemical bonds, such as carbon-oxygen (C-O) and nitrogen-oxygen (N-O) bonds. It is particularly effective in breaking aryl ethers and in the deoxygenation of epoxides. The term aluminium iodide is most commonly associated with aluminium triiodide or its dimeric form. However, aluminium monoiodide (AlI) also exists within the aluminium-iodine system. Despite this, AlI is thermodynamically unstable at room temperature and tends to decompose into the triiodide form. A notable derivative of aluminium monoiodide is a cyclic adduct formed with triethylamine, which has the composition Al₄I₄(NEt₃)₄. From a safety perspective, the hydrolysis of aluminium triiodide releases hydrogen iodide (HI), a highly corrosive substance. Additionally, as a Lewis acid, aluminium iodide can act as a skin irritant and should be handled with appropriate precautions.
